subject: maths
question:
The graphs of the equations

4x + (1)/(3)y = (8)/(3) and (1)/(2)x + (3)/(4)y + (5)/(2) = 0 intersect at a point P. The point P also lies on the graph of the equation:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Simplify given equations to standard linear form ax + by = c.

Equation 1: 4x + y/3 = 8/3 → 12x + y = 8

Equation 2: x/2 + 3y/4 = −5/2 → 2x + 3y = −10

Solve quickly: Multiply Eq 1 by 3 and subtract: (36x + 3y) − (2x + 3y) = 24 − (−10) ⇒ 34x = 34 ⇒ x = 1, y = −4.

Check options with P(1, −4): Option (2) ⇒ 3(1) − (−4) − 7 = 3 + 4 − 7 = 0.

**∴ The correct answer is 3x − y − 7 = 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Equation 1: 4x + y/3 = 8/3

Equation 2: x/2 + 3y/4 + 5/2 = 0

**Formula Used:**

Substitution or Elimination method for linear equations in two variables.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/89f1c28e3d5c3ea543a5e7984e4146f19404a5b90656f0468d83295b3f18a5c7.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ From Equation 1: 12x + y = 8 ⇒ y = 8 − 12x ... (i)

⇒ From Equation 2: (2x + 3y + 10) / 4 = 0 ⇒ 2x + 3y = −10 ... (ii)

⇒ Substitute (i) into (ii): 2x + 3(8 − 12x) = −10

⇒ 2x + 24 − 36x = −10

⇒ −34x = −10 − 24 ⇒ −34x = −34 ⇒ x = 1

⇒ Substitute x = 1 in (i): y = 8 − 12(1) = −4

⇒ Intersection Point P = (1, −4)

⇒ Test Option (2): 3x − y − 7 = 3(1) − (−4) − 7 = 3 + 4 − 7 = 0

**∴ The correct answer is 3x − y − 7 = 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Nature of Roots for Linear Equations

For a system a₁x + b₁y = c₁ and a₂x + b₂y = c₂, if a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂, the lines intersect at exactly one point (Consistent system).

Parallel and Coincident Lines

If a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂, lines are parallel (No solution). If a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂, lines are coincident (Infinite solutions).

Point-Line Relationship

A point (x₀, y₀) lies on a graph of an equation if substituting the coordinates into the equation satisfies the equality f(x₀, y₀) = 0.</p
